message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “soft” card because it can be counted as either **1** or **11**, whichever gives the best advantage to the hand without causing a bust.

Key points:

| Situation | How the Ace is treated |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Single Ace in a hand** | You may choose to count it as 1 or 11. Most players will count it as 11 unless doing so would cause the total to exceed 21, in which case it becomes 1. |
| **Two Aces (a pair)** | If you’re allowed to split pairs, you can split the two Aces into separate hands. Each new hand starts with one Ace. In many casinos, when you split Aces you receive only one additional card per hand (no further draws). |
| **After splitting Aces** | Some casinos allow you to double down on a split Ace, but others do not. |
| **Dealer’s rule** | The dealer usually hits on a soft 17 (A‑6) and stands on a hard 17 (any other combination totaling 17). |

So, the Ace’s flexibility—being worth 1 or 11—makes it a powerful card that can turn a weak hand into a strong one or prevent a bust.
